textContent.text: There are many reasons why voters may choose to remain independent rather than joining a political party. Some voters may not have political views that neatly align with one party. They may have a mixture of views from both major parties, or believe other things entirely. So, they may change the party they vote for with every election, or they may choose not to vote at all. Or, they may choose to vote on only one single issue that's important to them.

Although independent voters don't belong to a party, they usually still vote for major party candidates. Most independent voters prefer one party over the other, although not enough to join the party. But they still tend to vote for that party regularly over many elections.

textContent.text: There are many reasons why voters may choose to remain independent rather than joining a political party. Some voters may not have political views that neatly align with one party. They may have a mixture of views from both major parties, or believe other things entirely. So, they may change the party they vote for with every election, or they may choose not to vote at all. Or, they may choose to vote on only one single issue that's important to them.

Although independent voters don't belong to a party, they usually still vote for major party candidates. Most independent voters prefer one party over the other, although not enough to join the party. But they still tend to vote for that party regularly over many elections.
